name: Портреты по способу, принятому автором 30.09.2026 (тест 2 Гримсы): по одному герою
style: Art style: our game's hand-painted dark-fantasy character art, exactly like the attached reference paintings of our heroes: painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes, soft painterly edges, semi-realistic human proportions and anatomy, a naturally proportioned head and hands, subtle realistic facial modelling, deep atmospheric shadows, a dark moody background with depth and soft focus, crisp rim light along the edges, glowing crystals and embers throwing colored light upward from below, dust motes in the light. NOT a cartoon, NOT a caricature, NOT chibi, no oversized head, no thick black outlines, no cel shading, no flat comic colors; no photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, rendering, proportions, lighting and color handling of the attached reference paintings, but do NOT copy their subjects, faces, costumes or composition.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no writing on paper, books, maps or stones, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no name plate, no dark band at the bottom, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood, no monsters in the picture. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes. No generic fantasy face; the hero does not look away — the eyes look into the camera.

heroes.frame: Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up; the bottom edge cuts the body at the hips; no knees, no feet. The camera is a little below the chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. THE HERO LOOKS AT THE VIEWER: the body is turned three-quarters, but the head turns to us and the eyes look straight into the camera, meeting the eyes of the person who looks at the picture — a living person with a story. The face is the heart of the picture: in the upper third, well lit from below, with an expression that tells who they are. Give the face exactly the specific features described below — bone structure, eyes, nose, mouth, skin, scars, age — so that it looks like this one person and no one else. The pose is this hero's own signature moment from their story, with weight and intent — not a generic attack, not a generic stance. Clothing and objects are specific to their life, worn and personal, in a color palette of their own. The background is the place of their story, darker and softer than the figure. The lower edge sinks gradually into shadow — no band, no plate, nothing written.

jobs.title: Рунна Литейщица — по принятому способу: глава «Последняя форма»
jobs.subject: Subject: Runna the Founder, a dwarf woman, a foundry worker and a mage of the Fire school. Who she is: she chose the strange twice: she learned fire from a northern mage who came with a caravan, and she worked with that fire in the foundry. Her metal always ran true, because she poured on the out-breath: in-breath, pause, stream, the way the elf taught the founders to breathe. Her apprentice, a young northerner, went down into the lower drifts after a comrade and never came up. Her last casting was a memorial plaque for those the deep has taken: his name was the first she cast on it, and below it she left space, in case they decide there is room for her too. The moment: she pours the molten metal of that plaque, on the out-breath, guiding the glowing stream with her own fire; her lips are pursed in a slow steady breath, and she looks straight at you, grieving and steady. Character, written in her body: fierce, grieving, exact; a craftswoman who holds her breath and her grief with the same discipline; her shoulders braced, her hands perfectly steady. Her face, make it hers alone: a dwarf woman of about fifty; an oval face with a heavy, prominent brow ridge; no eyebrows at all, burnt away years ago in the foundry, the skin there shiny and smooth; grey-green eyes rimmed with a faint glow of fire; a straight strong nose; full lips pursed in a slow out-breath, cheeks slightly hollowed; a scorched bare patch at her hairline; dark auburn hair twisted into a tight knot under a leather foundry hood pushed back; soot smudges across her cheekbones; a fine silver scar at the corner of her mouth. No beard. Short, broad, powerful arms. Her clothing, her own palette of scorched leather brown, blackened iron and molten orange: a heavy leather foundry coat with iron-studded shoulders, a leather face shield pushed up onto her hood, thick gauntlets, one of them pulled off and hanging from her belt, a northern fire-mage's red cord bracelet on her bare wrist, the gift of her teacher. Pose, standing, the moment of pouring: she stands turned three-quarters at a long stone casting mould; she has exactly two arms: her near hand, in a gauntlet, tilts a glowing crucible by its long iron handle; her far hand is bare and raised, fingers spread, and the stream of molten metal bends and flows smoothly along her command, wrapped in living flame; her head is turned to us and her eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell her story: (1) the long stone mould on the floor, its face angled away from the viewer, glowing where the metal runs in, no letters visible; (2) the red cord bracelet of the northern fire; (3) behind her the great dark foundry: chains, crucibles, a furnace mouth roaring; (4) a young man's leather apron hanging empty on a hook by the furnace. Place and light: a deep dwarven foundry; the molten metal and the living flame light her face from below in orange and gold; sparks, heat haze and smoke in the air.

jobs.title: Эйвинд Ученик Горна — по принятому способу: глава «Смена без него»
jobs.subject: Subject: Eyvind Forge-Apprentice, a young northern human warrior, a fighter of the Fire school who strikes with a blade of burning Nitrium. Who he is: in the north he passed all three trials and carried a blade of red Nitrium, but the north measures a man by what he has made, and nobody makes things better than the dwarves, so he went to learn from them. In the mountain he became apprentice to the founder who poured on the out-breath and lived by the horn of the old woman who was never late. He laughed at the saying 'breathe like Haldur' only the first year. In his last shift he went down into the lower drifts after a comrade and dragged him to the lift cage, but there was not enough air for a second climb. He gave the comrade his second blade, let at least him rise, and sat down to breathe, slowly, counting. The moment: he stands at the lift cage in the bad air of the lower drift; the cage is rising behind him with his comrade in it; he has given away his second blade; he holds the remaining one and looks straight at you, calm, counting his breath, without regret. Character, written in his body: big, warm-hearted, stubborn, unafraid; his chest heaving slowly, his shoulders squared, the calm of a man who chose. His face, make it his alone: about thirty; a big, broad northern face with a strong square jaw and high flushed cheekbones; pale ice-blue eyes; a slightly crooked nose; thick flame-red hair, long, the sides braided tight to the skull in northern style, tied back with leather cords; a thick red beard with two small braids at the chin, each bound with a copper ring; three short parallel scars across his left cheek, the marks of the three northern trials; freckles; sweat and dust on his skin. His clothing, his own palette of grey-blue northern wool, dwarven leather brown and crimson: a dwarven founder's leather apron worn over a northern grey-blue wool tunic with a rough fur collar; heavy leather bracers; two crossed scabbards on his back, and one of them is empty. Pose, standing, the moment after the gift: he stands tall, body turned three-quarters; he has exactly two arms: his near hand holds his Nitrium blade point-down beside his leg, the blade glowing a deep crimson from within; his far hand grips the iron bar of the lift frame beside him; his head is turned to us and his eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell his story: (1) the empty scabbard on his back; (2) the three trial scars; (3) behind him the lift cage of iron bars rising up the dark shaft on its chain, a hand gripping the bars from inside; (4) a thick yellow haze of bad air low around the collapsed drift, broken timber props. Place and light: a lower drift deep in the mountain; the crimson glow of the Nitrium blade and red-orange Fire-school light from embers in the rock light his face from below; dust and yellow haze in the air.

jobs.title: Руммат Без Горы — по принятому способу: глава «Дорога»
jobs.subject: Subject: Rummat the Mountainless, an exiled dwarf, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: he was written into the list of the unreliable for carrying out more than was his, and a dwarf without a mountain is nobody; he could not go to the humans either. He settled at the foot of the mountain, where the gate can be seen, and every year he asked the gatekeeper to take a toll from him, as from a stranger; the gatekeeper answered that the law does not know the exiled. He kept the road to the mountain himself: he walked travellers safely to the gate, a scribe from the west on his ninth attempt, an elf woman with her tinctures. He lay down on that same road in the end. The moment: he stands on the road below the gate and holds out a toll coin to you, as if you were the gatekeeper: take it, as from a stranger. Proud and pleading at once. Character, written in his body: dignified, lonely, stubborn, loyal to a mountain that disowned him; his back straight, his chin up, his eyes wet but steady. His face, make it his alone: an old dwarf; a heavy, lined, sun-weathered face, darker than a mountain dwarf's from years under the open sky; sad, deep brown eyes under grey shaggy brows; a big crooked nose; his beard cut short and ragged, hacked off unevenly, the shame of the exiled; grey-brown hair long and unkempt; a torn earlobe on the left side where a guild ring was ripped out; a scar along the jaw. His clothing, his own palette of faded road-dust brown, grey and one old guild blue: a long weather-worn travelling coat, patched and dusty; under it an old dwarven guild tunic of faded blue with the guild marks cut away, leaving pale unstitched patches; heavy road boots, not visible; a road lantern on a pole. Pose, standing, the moment of the toll: he stands on the road, body turned three-quarters toward the mountain; he has exactly two arms: his near hand is held out toward us, palm up, a single worn coin on it; his far arm holds a heavy round shield, a makeshift one of rough planks and stone bound with iron, without any guild emblem, leaning against his side; his head is turned to us and his eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell his story: (1) the pale patches on his tunic where the guild marks were cut away; (2) the torn earlobe; (3) the hacked-short beard; (4) behind him the winding road climbing up the mountainside to a great gate far above, lit and closed; a tiny hut at the foot of the mountain. Place and light: the road at the foot of a lone dwarven mountain at dusk; amber-orange Earth-school light rises from cracks in the road stones and lights his face from below; the warm tiny glow of the gate far above; dust in the air.

jobs.title: Бера Свечница — по принятому способу: глава «Последняя свеча»
jobs.subject: Subject: Bera the Candle-Keeper, a dwarf woman, a healer of the Earth school who keeps the lights of the dead. Who she is: in the deepest hall of Karoksorr stands the cradle, and there too, in niches, stand the dwarven dead, facing the work. She lit their candles and said the dead dwarves are the best neighbours: they never argue and never come late. One day the flames in the far niches began to lean down, toward the cracks in the floor; the hall's guard said it was a draught, and she did not believe him. The moment: she stands in the deep hall holding up her candle, whose flame bends down toward the cracks in the floor, and looks straight at you, calm and knowing, as if to say: it is not a draught. Among her people, one leaves standing. Character, written in her body: gentle, dry-humoured, brave, unhurried; her posture upright and still, a small wry smile. Her face, make it hers alone: a dwarf woman of middle age; a soft, pale, heart-shaped face that has seen little sun; large dark eyes with faint dark circles beneath from long vigils; a small upturned nose; a small scar through her lower lip; black hair streaked with grey, worn in a single long plait over her shoulder, with drops of old candle wax caught in it; a dark grey wool veil over her head. No beard. Short and sturdy. Her hands: small, with shiny pale wax burns on the fingertips. Her clothing, her own palette of dark grey wool, candle gold and pale wax white: a long dark grey wool robe with a hood-veil; a belt hung with bundles of thin candles and a small brass snuffer; a leather satchel of fresh candles. Pose, standing, the moment of the leaning flame: she stands turned three-quarters in the hall; she has exactly two arms: her near hand holds up a tall thick candle in a brass holder at chest height, its flame bending strangely downward; her far hand is raised, palm open toward the niches, with a soft warm amber light of healing around her fingers; her head is turned to us and her eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell her story: (1) the flame of her candle bending down, toward the floor; (2) behind her, a curving wall of tall niches, in each a still, stone-grey shrouded figure standing upright like a statue, faces calm and serene, lit by small candles; (3) thin cracks in the stone floor with a faint glow, where the flames lean; (4) the wax in her hair and the burns on her fingertips. Place and light: the deepest hall of a dwarven mountain, vast and dark, rows of niches with small candles; the candlelight and soft amber Earth-school light from the cracks light her face from below; still air, a few motes of dust drifting down.

jobs.title: Назир Пепельный — по принятому способу: глава «Чужие мёртвые»
jobs.subject: Subject: Nazir the Ashen, a human fire mage of the College, who sees off the dead of Endalor. Who he is: he came to Endalor at the call of the Temple of Fire and saw off the dead from the edge of the city's disc: in Endalor they burn everyone who bears the mark of a resident, and it is the cleanest work in the city. When the deep hall of the dwarven mountain burned out, the dwarves for the first time called a fire mage, to teach their own to keep fire at the niches. He taught for a year and left without thanks: dwarves thank by trade, and he had nothing to trade. He died at home, at the edge, and asked his apprentice to wait for the wind. The moment: he stands at the very edge of the city at dusk, ash rising from his open hands into the wind, and looks straight at you, serene, with the quiet compassion of a man who has seen off thousands. Character, written in his body: serene, ascetic, compassionate, tired and unafraid; his posture upright and relaxed, his face soft. His face, make it his alone: about sixty; dark brown skin; a lean, long, ascetic face with a high forehead and hollow cheeks; deep-set dark eyes with long lashes, grey with fine ash; grey eyebrows; a thin, closely trimmed white-grey beard; a shaved head with a smudge of grey ash across the forehead, the mark of his work; laughter lines at the corners of his eyes; old small burn scars on the backs of his hands. His clothing, his own palette of ash grey, charcoal and ember orange: a long ash-grey College robe with a charcoal-dark stole, its hem singed; a narrow ember-orange sash; a small brass censer hanging from his belt, trailing a thin line of smoke; simple leather sandals, not visible. Pose, standing, the moment of the wind: he stands at the edge, body turned three-quarters toward the open sky; he has exactly two arms: both hands are held before him at chest height, cupped and opening, and grey ash with tiny glowing embers lifts from his palms and streams away on the wind; a small calm flame of the Fire school burns in the hollow of his near palm; his head is turned to us and his eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell his story: (1) the ash and embers streaming away on the wind; (2) the ash mark on his forehead; (3) behind him the edge of the city: a low stone parapet and, beyond it, open dusk sky and a deep void below the edge, with a funeral pyre burning low on a stone platform nearby; (4) the brass censer at his belt. Place and light: the edge of the city of Endalor at dusk, wind blowing; the flame in his palm and the glowing embers light his face from below in warm orange; cool violet dusk sky behind; ash drifting in the air.
